period_status: Favored recurrence from two TESS eclipse centers assuming 22 cycles, supported by four ASAS-SN nights. The 97.86-day alias remains possible.
claim_basis: earlier public machine or TESS pipeline detection
prior_evidence: Kostov et al. (2025) machine-selected Table 2 and a TESS threshold-crossing event. No prior vetted eclipse or matching ephemeris found at the tested periods.
interpretation: Two roughly seven-hour eclipses have median in-window SAP depths of 27.6% and 28.6% in sectors 15 and 55. The deepest individual PDCSAP samples reach 40.4% and 40.6%. Both difference images fall 0.3 arcsec from the host with no flux-capable Gaia neighbour. The TIC radius is 2.66 ± 0.12 solar radii, so an eclipse this deep favors a stellar companion. Four ASAS-SN nights favor a 48.93-day recurrence. A secondary eclipse and a unique orbital period remain unestablished.
